title: When the Harbor Sings
premise: In 1912, on a storm-battered Atlantic coast, widowed lighthouse keeper Paloma Okonkwo tends her light and keeps to herself, hiding the fact that she has been quietly sheltering deserters and debt-fleeing fishermen in the keeper's cottage for years. When the army requisitions the harbor town to build a fortified breakwater, every resident's name is entered into a requisition ledger that determines who may stay, who must labor, and who gets passage out — and Paloma discovers her late husband's name was never legally recorded, making her claim to the light itself void. As the great storms of autumn close in, she is forced to choose which of her two remaining family members — her ailing sister-in-law Adaeze or her headstrong nephew Tomas — takes the last berth on the evacuation ship. In the end, Paloma gives up her own place, burns the ledger during the final storm, and escapes by sea with both of them, guiding other townsfolk through the black water by the light she refuses to let die.
about_author: Beatrix Villalobos is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs and coastal requisition records from the early twentieth century. She writes historical fiction about women whose labor kept the edges of the world running and whose names rarely made the ledgers.

chapters.title: The Light Keeps Its Own Hours
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Establishes her solitary routine tending the light after her husband Emeka's death three years prior, her careful invisibility in town, and the small kindnesses — extra oil, a warm meal — that hint at secrets. Emotional beat: grief worn as competence; loneliness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Holds
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A storm forces her to open the cellar to a half-drowned stranger, revealing the deserter network she inherited from Emeka. Her sister-in-law Adaeze helps without being asked. Emotional beat: fear braided with purpose; the first crack in her isolation.

chapters.title: Gray Ships at First Light
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The boy watches army transports anchor in the harbor and runs to warn his aunt. Soldiers post notices: the town is requisitioned, all residents to be registered. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread; childhood ending at the waterline.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the registration table, a young clerk named Ivo records names, trades, and claims. Paloma learns Emeka's keeper's license was never transferred — on paper, the light belongs to no one. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under a woman who thought she stood on solid stone.

chapters.title: Adaeze Counts the Days
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Ill and failing, Adaeze privately reckons what her sickness will cost the family when the army sorts the useful from the burdensome. She begins teaching Tomas the family recipes and stories. Emotional beat: love expressed as preparation for absence.

chapters.title: Ivo's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The clerk, himself conscripted from a fishing family, recognizes Paloma's name from old supply manifests and realizes the ledger he serves erases people like her. He falsifies one small entry and hates himself for how little it costs him. Emotional beat: complicity examined; conscience waking.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Soldiers occupy the lighthouse gallery for a signal station but leave her the lamp room — the light is 'strategic.' She must now feed and house officers while hiding fugitives below. Emotional beat: performing obedience while committing quiet treason.

chapters.title: The Berth List
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Orders arrive: one evacuation ship before winter, berths assigned by ledger priority. Ivo sees how the arithmetic condemns the old, the sick, the unregistered. He copies the list and burns the copy. Emotional beat: horror at tidy handwriting.

chapters.title: Tomas Runs the Bluffs
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tasked with carrying messages between the cottage and sympathetic fishermen, Tomas is nearly caught by a patrol and hides in a sea cave, where he finds supplies someone left years ago — evidence the network is older than he knew. Emotional beat: pride and terror arriving together.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Barometers fall; the first great storm approaches weeks early. The army orders the light darkened to confuse enemy ships, but dark water means wrecked fishing boats full of townsfolk. Paloma must decide whether to disobey a direct order. Emotional beat: duty inverted — the law now demands darkness.

chapters.title: The Night She Lit It Anyway
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, intercut with boats at sea. She lights the lamp against orders; lives are saved; an officer suspects but cannot prove it. Ivo covers for her in the logbook. Emotional beat: defiance as devotion; the harbor singing its gratitude in foghorn blasts.

chapters.title: What Adaeze Asks
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Knowing the berth list is coming, Adaeze asks Paloma to promise the seat to Tomas — and asks something harder: that Paloma stop choosing duty over living. Emotional beat: a dying woman granting permission to be happy.

chapters.title: The Officer's Eye
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Captain Reyes, sharp and not unkind, interviews Paloma about the irregularities in the light's records. Their conversation becomes a duel of definitions: what makes a keeper legitimate — paper or work? Emotional beat: respect across a line neither can cross.

chapters.title: A Name in Wet Ink
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Pressured to finalize the berth list, Ivo adds Paloma's name using Emeka's license number, forging legitimacy. He knows discovery means prison — or worse. Emotional beat: a small man doing a large thing, shaking.

chapters.title: Three Names, One Seat
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The final count comes down: one unclaimed berth remains, and the ledger lists Adaeze, Tomas, and Paloma herself as candidates. The choice she dreaded arrives wearing official seals. Emotional beat: love forced through the narrow gate of arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Cave Network
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas discovers the army plans to sweep the caves before departure, netting every hidden fugitive. He races the tide home with the news. Emotional beat: a child carrying adult weight, running faster than fear.

chapters.title: Burning the Ledger
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On the eve of evacuation, with Reyes closing in, Paloma and Ivo steal into the records office during a blackout drill and burn the requisition ledger — erasing the town's names so no one can be sorted, ranked, or abandoned. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, paid for in fire.

chapters.title: The Last Storm
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The greatest storm of the year strikes as the ship prepares to sail; the harbor road floods; soldiers and townsfolk alike cling to the same ropes. Paloma keeps the light burning through it all. Emotional beat: catastrophe dissolving every category but human.

chapters.title: Which Family Member
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the gangplank, the berth question resolves itself: Adaeze is too weak to board without help, and the manifest allows only two. Paloma puts Adaeze and Tomas aboard and stays behind with the light. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely, grief and certainty in one breath.

chapters.title: Keeper of No One's Light
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Alone through the storm's tail, she guides a final boatload of stragglers — including a wounded Reyes, whom she saves without hesitation — out past the shoals. Emotional beat: mercy as the truest form of keeping.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Ashore in the north, Tomas and Adaeze wait at a strange dock until a small boat appears through fog, running dark, steered by a figure they'd know anywhere. Emotional beat: hope held past all reason, then answered.

chapters.title: When the Harbor Sings
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue. Reunited in a free coastal village, the family builds a new life; Ivo arrives with the salvaged register of everyone the ledger tried to erase, and they read the names aloud each year. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt not by papers but by witness; the harbor's song finally theirs.
